smell: Two concurrent `okdctl deploy` or `okdctl destroy` invocations in the same project root both point at `infrastructure/terraform/environments/<env>/terraform.tfstate` with no Go-side barrier. Terraform itself takes a local-backend lock only around individual sub-commands (init/plan/apply/destroy each relock), so a race between run A's plan step and run B's destroy step is not protected end-to-end. Nothing in okdctl's own orchestrator checks 'am I the only okdctl running?' — no pidfile, no flock, no stale-run detection.
severity_reason: rubric §4/data-loss — concurrent runs on the same state file can interleave at any terraform command boundary and corrupt state. Roadmap E1 filed; remains unimplemented.
fix_summary: Acquire a flock on `<projectRoot>/.okdctl.lock` at orchestrator entry (deploy/destroy/cleanup/update-ingress). Release on orchestrator exit and on ctx cancel. On contention, fail fast with 'another okdctl run is active (pid=N, started=T)' instead of racing. Track in roadmap E1.
rule_source: Terraform local-backend docs (per-command lock, not per-orchestration lock)
Go proverb: 'do not communicate by sharing memory; share memory by communicating' — single-writer invariant
must_preserve: existing terraform.Executor API; single-operator usage pattern

smell: StepDef has no 'already-done' precondition hook or checkpoint. If okdctl crashes mid-setup, the next run starts from step 1, repeating work or reconciling side-effects ad-hoc. Each step's idempotency is implicit — some steps check FileExists, others re-run unconditionally (GenerateManifests, Inject*). There is no declared `ReRunSafe bool` on StepDef and no on-disk checkpoint recording 'last-completed-step-id' that the next orchestrator run can skip to. InterruptSummary tells the user 'resume with okdctl deploy' but the resume re-runs from step 0.
evidence:
type StepDef struct {
    ID         StepID
    Name       string
    Desc       string
    NonFatal   bool
    SkipWhen   func() bool
    SkipReason string
    OnStart    func()
    Exec       func(ctx context.Context) error
    OnError    func(error)
}
severity_reason: Not blocker — re-running deploy is mostly harmless because most steps happen to be idempotent, but the implicit-idempotency contract is fragile. Upgrades to the ~30-step phase graph risk introducing a non-idempotent step that silently corrupts a partial deploy.
fix_summary: Option A (lightweight): add `ReRunSafe bool` on StepDef, default false, and require every StepDef to declare it (lint-time enforcement that a step sets ReRunSafe explicitly). Document the contract in step.go. Option B (heavier): add on-disk checkpoint at `<workDir>/.okdctl-progress.json` — StepResult list after each step, skipped on re-run when step.ID matches. Start with A — cheap, forces authors to think about idempotency at the StepDef level.
rule_source: Twelve-factor §disposability (processes should be resilient to crashes)
repo-counter-example: roadmap.md N10 'Ctrl-C partial-progress summary' shipped but no resume semantic
must_preserve: StepDef + BuildSteps canonical API; backward compat for existing StepDefs

smell: postinstall steps (cleanup-bootstrap, deploy-production-dns) are NonFatal and mutate cluster-external state (bootstrap VM destroyed via targeted tf apply, /etc/dnsmasq.d/*.conf replaced). If StepCleanupBootstrap succeeds but StepVerifyKubeVIP fails and StepDeployProductionDNS is skipped, the cluster is left with: bootstrap VM gone, kube-vip not verified, DNS still pointed at bootstrap. The user has no resume command specific to 'just the postinstall DNS step'. `okdctl update-ingress` handles the haproxy->LB-IP transition, not the bootstrap->kube-vip DNS swap this scenario needs.
severity_reason: Design debt not correctness bug: the staged NonFatal approach is intentional (degrade-gracefully to haproxy routing when kube-vip fails) but the resume story for 'finish postinstall DNS when kube-vip comes up later' is not documented and has no dedicated CLI path.
fix_summary: Two options: (a) add `okdctl postinstall --step=dns` subcommand that re-runs just the DNS sub-phase once kube-vip is confirmed healthy; or (b) expand update-ingress to handle the bootstrap->production DNS transition when it's still pointing at bootstrap IP. Prefer (b) since update-ingress already owns DNS re-deploys.
must_preserve: postinstall step ordering; NonFatal semantics that let partial success still give a usable cluster

smell: Provider.Provision delegates 100% to terraform — no Go-side retry on transient Proxmox API failures, no 409-already-exists handling beyond what the bpg/proxmox provider does internally. retrieveProvisionResult derives VM IPs from config (not from Proxmox), so eventual-consistency 'VM created but not yet listed' gaps are dodged by not querying Proxmox — but any future code that enumerates VMs from the API will need retry. The warn log 'run okdctl destroy to clean up' is the only recovery guidance on apply failure.
severity_reason: No direct Proxmox API calls on deploy/destroy path today (provider is pure-terraform); filed as a forward-looking note for when future code adds direct Proxmox queries.
fix_summary: Document the invariant in proxmox.go header: 'All Proxmox mutation MUST go through terraform.Executor. Direct HTTP calls are forbidden on deploy/destroy.' If/when status queries are added, use internal/download's retry helper (5xx/408/429 with exponential backoff, 4xx fail-fast).
rule_source: repo-counter-example: internal/download/retry.go (established retry pattern per roadmap U3)

smell: `okdctl cleanup` has only `--yes` with no typo-guard against the wrong config. Unlike `okdctl destroy` which requires `--confirm-cluster=<name>` when `--yes` is passed, cleanup stops and uninstalls haproxy/dnsmasq/apache, drops the VIP secondary IP, wipes terraform.tfstate.backup + .terraform.lock.hcl + bin-dir binaries (coreos-installer/terraform/oc/kubectl) without asserting the cluster name in scripted invocations. A script pointed at the wrong config uninstalls services on whichever bastion it hits. No `--dry-run` flag either — destroy and deploy both have one.
severity_reason: rubric §4/data-loss — scripted `--yes` run against the wrong config yields service-down (haproxy, dnsmasq, apache stopped + uninstalled) with no typo guard. Destroy already handles this class (destroy.go:81-93); cleanup is the asymmetric gap.
fix_summary: Mirror the destroy guards: add `--confirm-cluster` (required with `--yes`, must match cfg.Cluster.Name) and `--dry-run` (prints the list of services that would be stopped and files that would be removed without mutating). Promote the destroy.go guard block into a shared helper (e.g. `requireClusterConfirm(cfg, flag, fieldName)`) and call it from destroy + cleanup + any future destructive command.
must_preserve: existing cleanup.Kind enum; non-VM-destroying scope of cleanup

smell: `Provider.Provision` writes `<workDir>/tfplan` via Plan then applies it, but never sweeps the plan file on success or failure — only `destroyInfrastructure` calls `tf.Cleanup()`. After a successful deploy the operator is left with a stale `tfplan` that no longer matches state; after a failed apply it's doubly-stale. The bootstrap-cleanup path already solved this with `defer system.SafeRemove(planPath)` (postinstall/bootstrap.go:44-48) but provision did not adopt the pattern. `terraform.Executor.Cleanup` is the canonical sweeper.
severity_reason: Hygiene issue, not correctness: next provision run overwrites the stale tfplan via Plan. Flagged because symmetry with the bootstrap-cleanup fix (b804b2ec, now resolved) is trivial and the canonical sweeper already exists.
fix_summary: Add `defer func() { _ = p.terraformExec.Cleanup() }()` immediately after the Plan call succeeds in `Provider.Provision`, matching the bootstrap.go pattern. Plan file removal on failure also helps operators inspecting `<workDir>` after a failed apply because nothing stale is left.
must_preserve: Provision apply semantics; terraform plan file as the source of truth during the plan->apply window
